idiom_name: routing table: ordered (predicate -> destination channel) rules plus a stateless routing loop
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: consume from the input channel, evaluate an ordered rule list against message metadata (never by parsing the body), and republish the message unchanged to the selected destination. Keep the rules declarative and external to the router code so they can be reviewed and changed without touching the participants, and always define a default branch that sends unmatched messages to an Invalid Message Channel or Dead Letter Channel rather than dropping them. Make the router stateless so several instances can share the input channel, and emit per-route counters so misrouting is visible. When rules must change at runtime the plain router is the wrong pattern - move to a Dynamic Router; when the recipients are data, to a Recipient List.
code_sketch:
rules = [(m.type == "order.created", "orders.payment"),
         (m.type == "order.shipped", "orders.fulfilment")]
loop:
    msg = inbound.receive()
    for matches, destination in rules:          # ordered, first match wins
        if matches(msg):
            outbound[destination].send(msg)      # unmodified
            break
    else:
        dead_letter.send(msg, "no-route")        # never drop silently
pitfalls: Routing on payload content instead of stable metadata couples the decision to the message schema and turns the router into a parser.
No default branch: unmatched messages disappear without a trace.
Sharing mutable routing state across worker threads or router instances makes the decision non-deterministic.

Overlapping predicates without documented precedence let a newly added broad rule steal traffic from a specific route; make predicates mutually exclusive or encode and test explicit first-match/priority order.

Treating a no-match as success turns an invalid or novel message into a silent loss; send it to an Invalid Message Channel or Dead Letter Channel with the route key and rule-set version for diagnosis.

Switching mutable routing configuration non-atomically lets workers disagree during rollout; publish immutable, versioned rule snapshots and activate them atomically, or use a Dynamic Router when live updates are required.
